doc.title: Jane Jarvis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: New York jazz scene and producing for Muzak
summary: Her first New York job was with Milt Hinton and Osie Johnson; she later joined Muzak, rising to vice president and producing over 300 recordings with jazz musicians.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Well good. Now when you got into New York and a different atmosphere, were you able to get into the jazz scene? What was that like?

Well I’d only been in New York 24 hours and the first job I had was with Milt Hinton. And Osie Johnson was on drums. And I thought, oh, I’ve got it made. Well I can’t tell you how long I waited for a job after that. But then I did, I was engaged by Muzak Corporation. And I graduated from programmer until I became a producer and then I became the vice president. So that’s another whole career in music.
Wow. So you got to bring in some—

And so I met all the jazz musicians you know, although many of them I knew before like Clark Terry. But I produced a number of albums, or CDs we call them now, that they are on. It gave me an opportunity to arrange and to compose.
